dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: Every transfer handover (refine, specs, execute) starts with /clear, which drops the session back to the main checkout, so the leg command that follows it (e.g. `/spec:propose add-session-handover` in tests/golden/trunk-one-docket.md) runs in the wrong tree unless the user first cds by hand.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Each goal is an observable output or behaviour: the in-bay, trunk, and post-bay session handovers end in `/waybill:next <branch>/<leg>` instead of a `cd` fence plus the raw command, and that line enters the bay and runs the booking's command only when the leg is still the next one.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: The user approved the check list: `npm test`, greps against the goldens that fail on today's tree, allowed-tools and living-spec greps, and one judgment call in a live session; an interview spike (a headless `claude -p` running EnterWorktree({path}) then Skill) confirmed that the mechanism works.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: The user picked every transfer handover with a bay, in session output only (plain CLI output keeps its `cd`); through legs, the pre-bay ideate leg, automating /clear, and reliance on frontmatter model routing are explicitly out.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The conflict with command-surface's 'verbatim rendering, one keyed exception' rule is resolved by adding a second keyed exception (renderer-emitted `ENTER BAY:` / `RUN:` headings) to the living spec, and the branch-vs-leg split is unambiguous because git forbids `feat/foo` and `feat/foo/execute` from coexisting as branches.

problem: Waybill's transfer handover (the refine, specs, and execute legs) starts with `/clear`. In practice `/clear` drops the Claude Code session back to the main checkout, so the leg command pasted after it — `/spec:apply add-thing` — runs against the trunk, not the bay whose docket it belongs to. The user has to notice this, cd or restart in the bay, and re-orient before every leg.

The CLI can already resolve a docket from anywhere (`waybill next <branch>` looks the bay up in the fleet), but the `/waybill:next` slash command ignores its arguments, and nothing in the plugin can move a session into a bay. The trunk and `/waybill:bay` handovers still end in a `cd` fence that a Claude Code session can't act on.
goals: A transfer handover rendered for a session (markdown) for a docket with a bay ends in `/waybill:next <branch>/<leg>`, preceded by `/clear`, `/model <m>`, `/effort <e>`, whether it was printed inside the bay, from the trunk, or by `/waybill:bay` after cutting — and the session markdown shows no `cd` fence.
`/waybill:next <branch>/<leg>`, run from any checkout of the repo, enters that branch's bay with EnterWorktree and invokes the booking's command (with its argument) there, in one command.
`/waybill:next <branch>` (no leg) enters the bay and shows its waybill, running nothing.
A stale leg token (the named leg is not the docket's next leg) runs nothing: it shows the current waybill with a one-line note naming the actual next leg.

If the bay can't be entered (the EnterWorktree tool is denied, or the bay sits outside `.claude/worktrees` while the session is already in another worktree), the command runs nothing and falls back to today's waybill with its `cd` line.

decisions.decision: The token after the branch is the leg id (`feat/foo/execute`)
decisions.rejected: A command-derived slug (`feat/foo/spec-apply`), or no token (always run the next leg)
decisions.reason: Leg ids are a closed set (so the split is reliable) and stay stable when a bay overrides the booking's command; no token would lose the show-vs-run split

decisions.decision: Keep /model and /effort lines in the handover before `/waybill:next <branch>/<leg>`
decisions.rejected: A 2-line handover relying on the leg command's frontmatter to set the model
decisions.reason: A spike showed `claude -p` ignores `model:` frontmatter even on a direct call, so nothing was verifiable; and spec:apply is `model: inherit`, so frontmatter can't carry the execute booking's opus

decisions.decision: A stale leg token refuses: switch in, show the current waybill with a note, run nothing
decisions.rejected: Run the named leg anyway, or ask
decisions.reason: A stale paste must never re-run finished work, and the fresh handover is right there

decisions.decision: Use the new line on every transfer handover with a bay (in-bay, trunk, /waybill:bay) in session output; plain output keeps `cd`
decisions.reason: All three strand the session the same way, and one handover style is simpler

decisions.decision: `/waybill:next <branch>` with no leg switches into the bay and shows the waybill
decisions.reason: Gives a clean show-vs-run split at almost no cost, because the CLI already resolves the branch

decisions.decision: If the bay can't be entered, show the waybill with its `cd` and stop
decisions.rejected: Run the leg in the current checkout
decisions.reason: Running spec:apply in the wrong tree is the one outcome that must not happen

decisions.decision: Record this as an ideation contract plus spec, editing the living command-surface spec directly
decisions.reason: It would duplicate the spec, and learnings.md records that phases sharing one tasks.md break autopilot's skip pre-pass
Both rewrite next.md's `!` line, and bang-line's non-zero-exit guard is what keeps the new error paths' Task visible

decisions.decision: The session switch uses EnterWorktree({path}); the CLI only emits the path
decisions.reason: Headless spikes confirmed that EnterWorktree({path}) moves the session from the main checkout and from one .claude/worktrees bay to another, and that a command invoked through Skill afterwards runs there and can Write, even with neither allowed-tools list naming Write

decisions.decision: ENTER BAY is keyed on an explicit argument, not only on the caller's location
decisions.rejected: Emitting ENTER BAY whenever the caller is outside the resolved bay
decisions.reason: The scope-creep critic showed the pre-fix trigger would move the session on a plain trunk /waybill:next and on the SELECT A DOCKET re-run, which no goal asked for

decisions.decision: The bang-line gate is a wait on another docket's merge
decisions.rejected: This contract merging bang-line and resolving its conflict
decisions.reason: Scope-creep critic: that merge belongs to the bang-line-exit-guard docket's acceptance

decisions.decision: The stale-leg note is a keyed renderer marker `NEXT LEG: <leg>`
decisions.rejected: A free-prose note (`... is not the next leg`)
decisions.reason: Success-criteria critic: a prose needle breaks on rewording and did not prove the note names the actual next leg

decisions.decision: The cd fallback reuses the ENTER BAY path already printed, with its exact text fixed by the living spec; no second waybill variant is rendered
decisions.rejected: Rendering a cd-bearing copy of the waybill in every ENTER BAY response
decisions.reason: Over-engineering critic: goal 5 needs only the path, which the Task already has

decisions.decision: Fold the /waybill:help walkthrough update into this effort
decisions.rejected: A separate follow-up after merge (the pre-change plan left help out of scope while it was unmerged)
decisions.reason: #12 landed after approval; shipping without it leaves the reference card contradicting the handover for a release
